title: Dedicated Capacity Q3 Blueprint: 'Slice-to-Stride' Pilot for Segmented Commitments & Canary Playbooks
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Background:
Redwood's Dedicated offering must support more granular reservation patterns for mid-market customers who want predictable latency but cannot justify a full dedicated pool. This ticket scopes a Q3 pilot—'Slice-to-Stride'—that tests segmented commitments (fractional pool slices), defines automated fallback / canary runbooks for autoscale failures, and surfaces billing/financial implications for accounting and pricing teams.

Objectives:
1) Define how to carve dedicated pools into 'slices' that can be reserved and billed independently while maintaining latency SLOs.
2) Implement a canary playbook for autoscale fast-fail scenarios (fallback to lower-cost model variants, warm pool warmers, and cross-region spillover).
3) Measure unit economics (cost per 1M tokens) and customer-visible metrics for the pilot cohort.
4) Create on-call runbooks and run a simulated incident rehearsal with operations.

Scope (what's in):
- API surface and console UI text for slice reservation creation (UX copy + guardrails).
- Autoscale policy variants for slice owners (min/max, surge corridor, cooldowns).
- Canary playbook automation hooks (policy switches, fallback routes, incident alert thresholds).
- Billing telemetry to compute per-slice usage and effective cost.

Out of scope (for the pilot):
- Full multi-tenant RBAC across slices (we'll rely on existing pool isolation).
- New legal contract language; commercial adjustments to be manual for pilot customers.

Deliverables:
- Spec document with design and API contract (link to Confluence in comments).
- Prototype console flow for slice creation and monitoring.
- Canary runbook with play-by-play steps and automation scripts.
- Telemetry dashboard showing SLOs, cost, and warm-pool utilization for pilot customers.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Miguel Torres (owner), Asha Raman (strategy), Priya Iyer (pricing)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Pilot slice creation flow validates and stores slice metadata and shows expected throughput and latency.
2) Autoscale policy can trigger fallback to pre-configured model variants with <5% request drop in lab canary.
3) Billing records reflect per-slice usage to within 1% accuracy vs. raw tokens.
4) Canary runbook executed in rehearsal with oncall and SRE, documented lessons logged.
5) Charter decision: continue/pivot/stop with clear criteria documented.
metrics: Cost per 1M tokens measured for pilot cohort
timeline: 2026-04-05: Prototype UI + autoscale policy hooks ready for QA
risks: Financial misestimation of per-slice cost leading to unattractive pricing
Unexpected latency regression from added policy routing
Complexity in billing attribution for shared GPU resources
Insufficient warm pool capacity during real surge causing customer-visible errors
